prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / background-extraction.
Edit target and visual authority: the attached reference image of a vintage acoustic guitar headstock in a warm vinyl listening room.
Produce a production-quality photorealistic isolated cutout of THAT SAME guitar headstock and a short neck segment. Preserve its rich figured dark walnut-brown wood, visible pores and fine scratches, aged warm brass tuning hardware, rounded ivory perimeter binding, six strings, and the same elegant vintage crown silhouette. Exactly three physically plausible tuning keys on each side, six total, with all knobs fully visible. Preserve the front-facing straight-on view and the dramatic but natural warm studio light, subtle material highlights, real depth, and realistic edge detail. Preserve the reference's three tuner rows and approximate relative positions: top row at 25% of object height, middle at 44%, bottom at 64%; the ivory nut near 90%.
Remove the entire listening-room background, lamp, records, furniture and all scenery. Use a genuine transparent alpha background, including clear holes between the keys and headstock. Keep only the complete headstock, all six tuning keys, the nut and a very short neck stub below the nut. Frame the entire object upright with a small transparent margin around every side; no clipped keys or crown. Portrait asset, roughly 2:3 proportions. No lettering, brand logos, tuner UI, note labels, buttons, meters or interface in the image. This is a photographic asset to place under real HTML controls, not an app mockup. No vector-art appearance, no flattened illustration, no cartoon, no plastic-looking generic 3D render, no additional pegs. Faithful realistic craft and tactile aged materials from the supplied image.
